# Microsoft vs. Alphabet: annual results, regulatory risk and outlook

## Executive Summary
- Alphabet had greater annual revenue: $402.836 billion versus Microsoft’s $331.839 billion. Microsoft grew faster, 18% versus 15%, although the fiscal periods differ. [1][2]
- Microsoft’s calculated operating margin was 46.8%, versus Alphabet’s 32.0%; its net margin was 40.3% versus 32.8%. [1][2]
- The EU accepted Microsoft’s commitments concerning Teams, according to secondary reporting. The retrieved evidence did not establish an Alphabet enforcement outcome or either company’s specific 10-K risk factors, so relative legal exposure cannot be assessed. [3–5]
- Microsoft guided to 18–19% fiscal second-quarter revenue growth; Alphabet maintained substantial 2026 capital-expenditure guidance. These are different measures. Recent attributable analyst commentary for neither company was verified. [6][7]

## Revenue growth and profitability

| Annual measure | Microsoft FY2026, ended June 30 | Alphabet FY2025, ended December 31 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Revenue | $331.839bn | $402.836bn |
| Revenue growth, year over year | 18% | 15% |
| Operating income | $155.237bn | $129.039bn |
| Operating margin, calculated | 46.8% | 32.0% |
| Net income | $133.749bn | $132.170bn |
| Net margin, calculated | 40.3% | 32.8% |

**Evidence:** Microsoft figures are from its 10-K; Alphabet’s are from its annual earnings release. Margins are calculated from reported income divided by revenue. [1][2]

**Key differences:** Alphabet’s revenue was $70.997bn greater, calculated, while Microsoft’s growth rate was 3 percentage points higher and its operating margin 14.8 points higher, using rounded figures. Microsoft generated slightly more net income despite lower revenue. These are comparisons of different 12-month periods, not a synchronized year. Net margins also reflect non-operating items and taxes. [1][2]

## Regulatory and antitrust risks

**Microsoft:** The European Commission opened an investigation in 2023 into Teams bundling with Office after a Slack complaint. The Wall Street Journal subsequently reported that the Commission accepted Microsoft’s commitments, settling the probe; the retrieved evidence does not establish an infringement. The decision date, exact commitments and appeal status were not retrieved. [3]

**Alphabet:** Its FY2025 10-K was located, but its specific risk-factor disclosures and a recent enforcement outcome were not substantiated in the retrieved evidence. [4]

**Key differences:** The Teams matter provides evidence of a Microsoft competition concern and a reported settlement, but the missing Alphabet enforcement evidence and missing specific risk factors for both companies preclude a meaningful comparison of exposure or remedies. Microsoft’s FY2026 10-K was also located, but the relevant risk-factor details were not verified. [1][3][4]

## Business outlook

**Microsoft:** Management guided fiscal Q2 2027 revenue to $96.0–$97.1bn, representing 18–19% growth, according to a secondary-hosted earnings-call transcript published October 29, 2026. [6]

**Alphabet:** Management maintained 2026 capital-expenditure guidance of $195–$205bn and expects spending to increase significantly in 2027, according to a secondary-hosted earnings-call transcript. Reuters also reported the 2027 expectation on October 29, 2026. [7][8]

**Key differences:** Microsoft’s cited guidance is a near-term revenue forecast; Alphabet’s is a capital-spending outlook. They cannot be compared as like-for-like growth forecasts. Both are management expectations, not assured outcomes. Neither company’s recent, dated analyst commentary was verified.

## Overall Comparison
Alphabet was larger by revenue in the reported years, while Microsoft grew faster and had higher operating and net margins. The available risk and outlook evidence is too incomplete or dissimilar to establish which company has lower regulatory exposure or a stronger forward outlook.

**Evidence gaps and uncertainty:** The specific 10-K risk factors for both companies, an Alphabet enforcement outcome, the detailed Microsoft Teams remedy and recent attributable analyst commentary for both companies were not verified. Guidance figures rely on secondary-hosted transcripts; the Alphabet transcript’s publication date was not retrieved. Fiscal periods differ. The absence of retrieved evidence is not evidence that risks or actions do not exist.

## Sources
1. Microsoft, FY2026 Form 10-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312526323660/msft-20260630.htm
2. Alphabet, FY2025 annual earnings release: https://s206.q4cdn.com/479360582/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/2025q4-alphabet-earnings-release.pdf
3. The Wall Street Journal, Teams commitments, date not retrieved: https://www.wsj.com/tech/eu-accepts-microsoft-commitments-to-address-competition-concerns-over-teams-66ace2fb?eafs_enabled=false
4. Alphabet, FY2025 Form 10-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000018/goog-20251231.htm
5. Microsoft, FY2026 Form 10-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312526323660/msft-20260630.htm
6. The Motley Fool, Microsoft earnings-call transcript, October 29, 2026: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/29/microsoft-msft-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript
7. Yahoo Finance, Alphabet earnings-call transcript, publication date not retrieved: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/GOOG.SW/earnings/GOOG.SW-Q3-2026-earnings_call-712854.html
8. Reuters, October 29, 2026: https://www.reuters.com/business/cash-is-king-investors-draw-new-battle-lines-ai-spending-boom-2026-10-29

## Research Question
What were Microsoft’s and Alphabet’s revenue growth and profitability in their latest reported fiscal years, compared with the preceding years?

## Key Findings
- [Fact] Microsoft’s FY2026 revenue rose 18% year over year to $331.839 billion; net income rose 31% to $133.749 billion. Its fiscal year ended June 30, 2026. [Microsoft 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312526323660/msft-20260630.htm)
- [Fact] Alphabet’s FY2025 revenue rose 15% year over year to $402.836 billion, and net income was $132.170 billion, versus $100.118 billion in FY2024. Its fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. [Alphabet earnings release](https://s206.q4cdn.com/479360582/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/2025q4-alphabet-earnings-release.pdf)
- [Interpretation] Microsoft’s calculated operating and net margins were approximately 46.8% and 40.3%, respectively, versus Alphabet’s 32.0% and 32.8%. The companies’ fiscal years end six months apart.

## Financial Facts
All amounts in US dollars; margins are calculated as income divided by revenue, except Alphabet’s operating margins, which are also reported rounded in its release.

| Measure | Microsoft FY2026 / FY2025, years ended June 30 | Alphabet FY2025 / FY2024, years ended December 31 |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $331.839bn / $281.724bn; FY2026 growth 18% ([SEC 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312526323660/msft-20260630.htm)) | $402.836bn / $350.018bn; FY2025 growth 15% ([IR release](https://s206.q4cdn.com/479360582/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/2025q4-alphabet-earnings-release.pdf)) |
| Operating income | $155.237bn / $128.528bn ([SEC 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312526323660/msft-20260630.htm)) | $129.039bn / $112.390bn ([IR release](https://s206.q4cdn.com/479360582/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/2025q4-alphabet-earnings-release.pdf)) |
| Net income | $133.749bn / $101.832bn ([SEC 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312526323660/msft-20260630.htm)) | $132.170bn / $100.118bn ([IR release](https://s206.q4cdn.com/479360582/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/2025q4-alphabet-earnings-release.pdf)) |
| Operating margin | 46.8% / 45.6%, calculated ([SEC 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312526323660/msft-20260630.htm)) | 32.0% / 32.1%, calculated ([IR release](https://s206.q4cdn.com/479360582/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/2025q4-alphabet-earnings-release.pdf)) |
| Net margin | 40.3% / 36.1%, calculated ([SEC 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312526323660/msft-20260630.htm)) | 32.8% / 28.6%, calculated ([IR release](https://s206.q4cdn.com/479360582/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/2025q4-alphabet-earnings-release.pdf)) |

## Sources
- Microsoft, FY2026 Form 10-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312526323660/msft-20260630.htm
- Microsoft, FY2026 fourth-quarter earnings release: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/earnings/fy-2026-q4/press-release-webcast
- Alphabet, FY2025 fourth-quarter and fiscal-year earnings release: https://s206.q4cdn.com/479360582/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/2025q4-alphabet-earnings-release.pdf
- Alphabet, 2025 annual report, SEC-hosted: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000130817926000344/goog014907-ars.pdf

## Caveats
As of November 7, 2026, the latest completed fiscal years differ: Microsoft’s ended June 30, 2026, and Alphabet’s ended December 31, 2025. Their results therefore cover different 12-month periods. Margins calculated from reported amounts are rounded to one decimal; Alphabet reports both operating margins rounded to whole percentages as 32%. Net income and net margin include non-operating items and taxes.

## Research Question
What regulatory and antitrust risks do Microsoft and Alphabet disclose in their latest annual risk factors, and what material recent enforcement actions affect each, as of November 7, 2026?

## Key Findings
- [Fact] **Microsoft — Teams:** The European Commission opened an antitrust investigation in 2023 into Microsoft’s bundling of Teams with Office after a Slack complaint. The Wall Street Journal reports that the Commission subsequently accepted Microsoft’s commitments, settling the probe. The bundling was the subject of an investigation, not an established infringement in the evidence retrieved. The decision date and detailed commitments were not retrieved. [WSJ](https://www.wsj.com/tech/eu-accepts-microsoft-commitments-to-address-competition-concerns-over-teams-66ace2fb?eafs_enabled=false)
- [Interpretation] Commitments addressing competition concerns may constrain Microsoft’s future conduct; their exact scope and any appeal cannot be assessed from the retrieved evidence.
- [Fact] **Alphabet:** Its FY2025 10-K was located, but the retrieved excerpt did not provide its specific regulatory risk factors or a recent enforcement outcome. No allegation, ruling, remedy or appeal can be reliably summarized from that excerpt. [SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000018/goog-20251231.htm)

## Financial Facts
- Microsoft’s latest located 10-K covers the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 (company filing: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312526323660/msft-20260630.htm).
- Alphabet’s latest located 10-K covers the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (company filing: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000018/goog-20251231.htm).
- Financial performance figures are outside this legal-risk brief.

## Sources
- Microsoft, FY2026 Form 10-K, SEC: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312526323660/msft-20260630.htm
- Alphabet, FY2025 Form 10-K, SEC: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000018/goog-20251231.htm
- The Wall Street Journal, Microsoft Teams antitrust settlement: https://www.wsj.com/tech/eu-accepts-microsoft-commitments-to-address-competition-concerns-over-teams-66ace2fb?eafs_enabled=false

## Caveats
The search excerpts did not yield the specific Item 1A regulatory and antitrust disclosures for either company, so those disclosures remain unverified here. The Teams decision date, exact remedies and appeal status were not retrieved; its reported outcome relies on a secondary source. No Alphabet enforcement action was substantiated in the retrieved results. Fiscal year-ends differ, and the latest located annual filings cover different periods.

## Research Question
What do Microsoft’s and Alphabet’s latest available management guidance and recent attributable analyst commentary indicate about their business outlooks, as of November 7, 2026?

## Key Findings
- [Fact] Microsoft management guided fiscal Q2 2027 revenue to $96.0–$97.1 billion, representing 18–19% growth. Its fiscal Q1 earnings release directs investors to the earnings call for guidance. The retrieved transcript was published October 29, 2026.
- [Fact] Alphabet management maintained 2026 capital-expenditure guidance at $195–$205 billion and expects spending to increase significantly in 2027. Reuters reported the 2027 expectation on October 29, 2026; the retrieved earnings-call transcript contains both statements.
- [Interpretation] The guidance points to continued expansion alongside substantial infrastructure investment, but neither company’s projection is an assurance of future results.
- [Fact] Recent, dated, individually attributable analyst outlook commentary for either company was not verified in the retrieved eligible sources.

## Financial Facts
- Microsoft: Fiscal Q2 2027 revenue guidance $96.0–$97.1 billion, 18–19% growth; management earnings-call transcript, published October 29, 2026: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/29/microsoft-msft-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript
- Alphabet: Calendar 2026 capital-expenditure guidance $195–$205 billion; Q3 earnings-call transcript hosted by Yahoo Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/GOOG.SW/earnings/GOOG.SW-Q3-2026-earnings_call-712854.html

## Sources
- Microsoft, FY2027 Q1 earnings release: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/earnings/fy-2027-q1/press-release-webcast
- The Motley Fool, Microsoft FY2027 Q1 earnings-call transcript, October 29, 2026: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/29/microsoft-msft-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript
- Alphabet, Q3 2026 earnings release filed with the SEC, October 28, 2026: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000080/googexhibit991q32026.htm

- Reuters, October 29, 2026: https://www.reuters.com/business/cash-is-king-investors-draw-new-battle-lines-ai-spending-boom-2026-10-29

## Caveats
The guidance figures are from secondary-hosted transcripts of management remarks, not independently verified against company-hosted call transcripts. The retrieved Alphabet transcript did not supply a publication date. No eligible source retrieved provided verified, dated analyst commentary for either company; that part of the question remains unanswered.
